transcript.speaker: Noa Levi
transcript.text: How has the last quarter been for the team?

transcript.speaker: Tom Avery
transcript.text: Honestly the queue is the pain. On a bad day we get two, three hundred alerts and maybe ten matter. My analysts spend the first hour of every shift clicking through duplicates.

transcript.speaker: Rachel Kim
transcript.text: And I have a board meeting every month where I have to explain our posture. Right now I take screenshots from Sentinel and paste them into slides. It takes me half a day.

transcript.speaker: Rachel Kim
transcript.text: Something I can hand to the board. Plain language. What happened, are our important systems safe, are we getting faster.

transcript.speaker: Tom Avery
transcript.text: For me, show me what's dangerous first. Sort by what it hits, not when it came in. A low on a test box should never be above a critical on a domain controller.

transcript.speaker: Tom Avery
transcript.text: One more thing. When a lead isn't around at night, we wait. I get why containment is locked, we had our own incident like that years ago. But tell the analyst who is on call so they can ping them.
